params.title: Dialogue History JSON
params.description:
Example of "User Prompt" and "Dialog History JSON" as a combined input: [{"role":"system","content":"Be precise and concise."},{"role":"user","content":"How many stars are there in our galaxy?"},{"role":"assistant", "content":"Astronomers estimate that the Milky Way contains between 100 billion and 400 billion stars."}]  
    
Example of using only "Dialog History JSON": [{"role":"system","content":"Be precise and concise."},{"role":"user","content":"How many stars are there in our galaxy?"}]

params.title: Max Tokens
params.description: The total number of tokens requested in "max_tokens" plus the number of prompt tokens sent in messages must not exceed the context window token limit of the requested model. If left unspecified, the model will generate tokens until it reaches either its stop token or the end of its context window. [More information](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/model-cards).

params.title: Frequency Penalty
params.description: Values above 1.0 penalize based on existing frequency, while 1.0 means no penalty. The range starts at 0 for no penalty and increases to discourage repeated tokens.

params.title: Presence Penalty
params.description: A value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics. Incompatible with frequency_penalty.

params.title: Search Recently Filter
params.description: Returns search results within the specified time interval - does not apply to images

params.title: Temperature
params.description: The amount of randomness in the response, valued between 0 inclusive and 2 exclusive. Higher values are more random, and lower values are more deterministic.

params.title: Top K
params.description: The number of tokens to keep for highest top-k filtering, specified as an integer between 0 and 2048 inclusive. If set to 0, top-k filtering is disabled. We recommend either altering top_k or top_p, but not both.

params.title: Top P
params.description: The nucleus sampling threshold, valued between 0 and 1 inclusive. For each subsequent token, the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. We recommend either altering top_k or top_p, but not both.

params.title: Response Format JSON
params.description: For correct functionality, make sure to properly structure your request in the User Prompt field (e.g. Please output a JSON object containing the following fields: first_name, last_name). Specify a valid JSON schema object to enable structured outputs in your request, for example: {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"first_name":{"type":"string"},"last_name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["first_name","last_name"]}}}. [More information](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/structured-outputs).

Web Search
params.description:
Enables the OpenRouter built-in server tool that searches the web for current information. The model decides when and how often to search. Works with any model that supports tool calling. If the selected model does not support tools calling, the legacy [Web Search Plugin](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/plugins/web-search) is used instead. 

Note: This option may increase cost due to external search usage (e.g. Exa, Parallel). 

Do NOT enable this option for models that already have built-in (native) web search, such as 'perplexity/sonar' or 'openai/gpt-4o-search-preview' - they do not require this setting. [Read more information](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/web-search).

params.title: Web Search: Engine
params.description:
Search engine for the server tool. 'auto' (default) uses native search if the provider supports it, otherwise Exa. 'native' forces the provider's built-in search. 'exa', 'parallel', and 'firecrawl' use external search services. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/web-search).

params.title: Web Search: Max Results
params.description:
Maximum number of search results to return per search call (1-25). Applies to Exa, Firecrawl, and Parallel engines; ignored with native provider search. Higher values provide more information but increase cost and token usage. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Search: Max Total Results
params.description:
Maximum total number of search results across all search calls in a single request. Useful for controlling cost and context size in agentic loops. Defaults to 50 when not specified. Ignored when Search Prompt is filled (legacy Web Search Plugin is used instead). 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Search: Context Size
params.description:
How much context to retrieve per result.

For models with built-in native web search (e.g. perplexity/sonar, openai/gpt-4o-search-preview), controls how much information is retrieved from each search. 

For other models: applies to Exa and Parallel engines; ignored with native provider search and Firecrawl. 

Ignored when Search Prompt is filled (legacy Web Search Plugin is used instead).

params.title: Web Search: Include Domains
params.description:
Limit search results to these domains. Supported by Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, and most native providers. Supports wildcards (e.g. `*.substack.com`) and path filtering (e.g. `openai.com/blog`). Cannot be used together with Search Exclude Domains. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Search: Exclude Domains
params.description:
Exclude search results from these domains. Supported by Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Anthropic, and xAI. Supports wildcards (e.g. `*.substack.com`) and path filtering (e.g. `openai.com/blog`). Cannot be used together with Search Include Domains. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Fetch
params.description:
Server tool gives any model the ability to fetch content from a specific URL. When the model needs to read a web page or PDF document, it calls the tool with the URL. OpenRouter fetches and extracts the content, returning text that the model can use in its response.

Only available for models that support tools. Do NOT enable this option for models that already have built-in (native) web search, such as 'perplexity/sonar' or 'openai/gpt-4o-search-preview' - they do not require this setting.[See the documentation.](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/web-fetch)

params.title: Web Fetch Parameters JSON
params.description:
Optional configuration object. For example: {"engine":"auto","max_uses":5,"max_content_tokens":30000,"allowed_domains":["openrouter.ai"],"blocked_domains":["example.com"]}. 

Available only when "Web Fetch" is enabled. [See the documentation.](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/send-chat-completion-request#request.body.tools.WebFetchServerTool)

params.title: Datetime
params.description: Enables the OpenRouter built-in server tool that returns the current date and time. Useful for prompts that require temporal awareness - scheduling, time-sensitive questions, or any task where the model needs to know the current date and time. Works with any model that supports tool calling. [Read more information](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/datetime).

params.title: Datetime Timezone
params.description:
IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/New_York", "Europe/London", "Asia/Tokyo"). Defaults to UTC. 

Available only when "Datetime" is enabled.

params.title: Reasoning Effort
params.description: OpenAI-style reasoning effort setting

params.title: Reasoning Max Tokens
params.description: Non-OpenAI-style reasoning effort setting. Cannot be used simultaneously with effort.

params.title: Reasoning Exclude
params.description: Whether to exclude reasoning from the response

params.title: Output JSON Schema
params.description:
Example: {"name":"two_parameters","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"first_parameter":{"type":"string","description":"Value for the first parameter"},"second_parameter":{"type":"string","description":"Value for the second parameter"}},"required":["first_parameter","second_parameter"],"additionalProperties":false},"strict":true}

You can use [this link](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses) to generate example for your query.

params.title: Grammar Output
params.description: If enabled, the response will be returned in a grammar format. If both parameters are enabled: "Structured Output" and "Grammar Output", grammar is prioritized.

params.title: Grammar
params.description: Custom grammar for text generation. Used only when "Grammar Output" is enabled. Accepts a string in **GBNF (GGML BNF)** format - an extended BNF grammar used by llama.cpp-compatible models. Example: root ::= "yes" | "no". Note: Not all models support this feature. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/send-chat-completion-request#request.body.response_format.ResponseFormatTextGrammar).

params.title: Max Completion Tokens
params.description: Integer format, maximum tokens in completion

params.title: Context Compression
params.description: If enabled, automatically compresses prompts that exceed the model's context size by removing or truncating messages from the middle until the prompt fits. Useful when perfect recall is not required. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/message-transforms).

params.title: Temperature
params.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or "Top P" but not both. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#temperature).

params.title: Frequency Penalty
params.description: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Controlling the repetition of tokens based on how often they appear in the input. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#frequency-penalty).

params.title: Presence Penalty
params.description: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Repeats specific tokens already used in the input. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#presence-penalty).

params.title: Repetition Penalty
params.description: Number between 0.0 and 2.0. Reduces the likelihood of the model repeating words or phrases. A higher value makes the output more varied by discouraging repetition. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#repetition-penalty).

params.title: Stop Sequences
params.description: Stop generation immediately if the model encounter any token specified in the stop array

params.title: Logit Bias
params.description: Adjusts the likelihood of specific tokens being selected by modifying their logits. Values range from -100 to 100. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#logit-bias). For example: In the 'Key' field, enter "-80", in the 'Value' field, enter "10".

params.title: Logprobs
params.description: Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned.

params.title: Top Logprobs
params.description: Number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability

params.title: Min P
params.description: Minimum probability for a token to be considered, relative to the probability of the most likely token. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#min-p).

params.title: Top P
params.description: Number between 0 and 1. An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with "Top P" probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or "Temperature" but not both. [Read mode](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#top-p).

params.title: Top A
params.description: Consider only the top tokens with "sufficiently high" probabilities based on the probability of the most likely token. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#top-a).

params.title: Top K
params.description: Limits the model’s choice of tokens at each step, making it choose from a smaller set. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#top-k).

params.title: Seed
params.description: Repeated requests with the same seed and parameters return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed for some models. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#seed).

params.title: Include Cache Control
params.description: More info [here](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching)

params.title: Cache Control TTL
params.description: Note: not all models support this feature. More info [here](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching).

params.title: Session ID
params.description: A unique identifier for grouping related requests (e.g., a conversation or agent workflow) for observability. Maximum 128 characters.

params.title: Tools JSON
params.description:
For example: [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"search_gutenberg_books","description":"Search for books in the Project Gutenberg library based on specified search terms","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"search_terms":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"List of search terms to find books in the Gutenberg library (e.g. ['dickens', 'great'] to search for books by Dickens with 'great' in the title)"}},"required":["search_terms"]}}}]  
    [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/tool-calling).

params.title: Tools Choice
params.description:
Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model. 

`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.

`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools.

`required` means the model must call one or more tools.

Specifying a particular tool via `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_rain_probability"}}` forces the model to call that tool.

`none` is the default when no tools are present. `auto` is the default if tools are present.

params.title: Providers Filter: Ignored Providers
params.description: Select providers that will be ignored for the request

params.title: Providers Filter: Allow Fallbacks
params.description: When enabled, if the primary provider is unavailable, the next best provider will be used. When disabled, only the primary or custom provider is used and an upstream error is returned if it is unavailable.

params.title: Providers Filter: Data Collection
params.description: If no available model provider meets the requirement, the request will return an error

params.title: Providers Filter: Enforce Distillable Text
params.description: If enabled, only models where the author has allowed distillation will be used.

params.title: Providers Filter: Preferred Max Latency
params.description: Preferred maximum latency in seconds. Allowed keys: p50, p75, p90, p99. All specified cutoffs must be met for an endpoint to be preferred. Endpoints above the threshold may still be used but are deprioritized in routing.

params.title: Providers Filter: Preferred Min Throughput
params.description: Preferred minimum throughput in tokens per second. Allowed keys: p50, p75, p90, p99. All specified cutoffs must be met for an endpoint to be preferred. Endpoints below the threshold may still be used but are deprioritized in routing.

params.title: Providers Filter: Quantizations
params.description: Filter providers by quantization level

params.title: Providers Filter: Require Parameters
params.description: Filter providers to only those that support the parameters you have provided. If disabled, providers receive only the parameters they support and ignore the rest

params.title: Providers Filter: Zero Data Retention
params.description: Restrict routing to only Zero Data Retention (ZDR) endpoints that do not retain prompts. If enabled, only endpoints that do not retain prompts will be used.

params.title: Providers Filter: Sort
params.description: Provider sorting strategy used when field 'Providers' is not specified. When set, no load balancing is performed

params.title: Providers Filter: Max Price Prompt
params.description: Maximum price in USD per million prompt tokens

params.title: Providers Filter: Max Price Completion
params.description: Maximum price in USD per million completion tokens

params.title: Auto Router Allowed Models
params.description: Use only when 'Auto Router' is enabled. List of model patterns to filter which models the auto-router can route between. Supports wildcards (e.g., 'anthropic/*' matches all Anthropic models, more examples [here](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/auto-router#pattern-syntax)). When not specified, uses the default supported models list.

params.title: Max Tokens (deprecated)
params.description: Use 'Max Completion Tokens' instead

params.title: Search Context Size (deprecated)
params.description: Use 'Web Search: Search Server Context Size' instead

params.title: Web Search Plugin (deprecated)
params.description: Use 'Web Search' instead

params.title: Search Prompt (Legacy Web Search Plugin)
params.description:
Custom instruction used to guide how web search results are incorporated into the model's response. Can be used to control citation style, summarization behavior, or formatting of sources. If this field is filled, web search uses the legacy Web Search Plugin instead of the OpenRouter Web Search server tool. 

Available only when "Web Search Plugin (deprecated)" is enabled.

params.title: Output JSON Schema
params.description:
Example: {"name":"two_parameters","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"first_parameter":{"type":"string","description":"Value for the first parameter"},"second_parameter":{"type":"string","description":"Value for the second parameter"}},"required":["first_parameter","second_parameter"],"additionalProperties":false},"strict":true}

params.title: Grammar Output
params.description: If enabled, the response will be returned in a grammar format. If both parameters are enabled: "Structured Output" and "Grammar Output", grammar is prioritized.

params.title: Grammar
params.description: Custom grammar for text generation. Used only when "Grammar Output" is enabled. Accepts a string in **GBNF (GGML BNF)** format - an extended BNF grammar used by llama.cpp-compatible models. Example: root ::= "yes" | "no". Note: Not all models support this feature. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/send-chat-completion-request#request.body.response_format.ResponseFormatTextGrammar).

params.title: Max Completion Tokens
params.description: Integer format, maximum tokens in completion

params.title: Context Compression
params.description: If enabled, automatically compresses prompts that exceed the model's context size by removing or truncating messages from the middle until the prompt fits. Useful when perfect recall is not required. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/message-transforms).

params.title: Temperature
params.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or "Top P" but not both. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#temperature).

params.title: Frequency Penalty
params.description: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Controlling the repetition of tokens based on how often they appear in the input. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#frequency-penalty).

params.title: Presence Penalty
params.description: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Repeats specific tokens already used in the input. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#presence-penalty).

params.title: Repetition Penalty
params.description: Number between 0.0 and 2.0. Reduces the likelihood of the model repeating words or phrases. A higher value makes the output more varied by discouraging repetition. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#repetition-penalty).

params.title: Stop Sequences
params.description: Stop generation immediately if the model encounter any token specified in the stop array

params.title: Logit Bias
params.description: Adjusts the likelihood of specific tokens being selected by modifying their logits. Values range from -100 to 100. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#logit-bias). For example: In the 'Key' field, enter "-80", in the 'Value' field, enter "10".

params.title: Logprobs
params.description: Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned.

params.title: Top Logprobs
params.description: Number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability

params.title: Min P
params.description: Minimum probability for a token to be considered, relative to the probability of the most likely token. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#min-p).

params.title: Top P
params.description: Number between 0 and 1. An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with "Top P" probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or "Temperature" but not both. [Read mode](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#top-p).

params.title: Top A
params.description: Consider only the top tokens with "sufficiently high" probabilities based on the probability of the most likely token. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#top-a).

params.title: Top K
params.description: Limits the model’s choice of tokens at each step, making it choose from a smaller set. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#top-k).

params.title: Seed
params.description: Repeated requests with the same seed and parameters return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed for some models. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters#seed).

params.title: Include Cache Control
params.description: More info [here](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching)

params.title: Cache Control TTL
params.description: Note: not all models support this feature. More info [here](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching).

params.title: Session ID
params.description: A unique identifier for grouping related requests (e.g., a conversation or agent workflow) for observability. Maximum 128 characters.

params.title: Tools JSON
params.description:
For example: [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"search_gutenberg_books","description":"Search for books in the Project Gutenberg library based on specified search terms","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"search_terms":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"List of search terms to find books in the Gutenberg library (e.g. ['dickens', 'great'] to search for books by Dickens with 'great' in the title)"}},"required":["search_terms"]}}}]  
    [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/tool-calling).

params.title: Tools Choice
params.description:
Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model. 

`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.

`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools.

`required` means the model must call one or more tools.

Specifying a particular tool via `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_rain_probability"}}` forces the model to call that tool.

`none` is the default when no tools are present. `auto` is the default if tools are present.

Web Search
params.description:
Enables the OpenRouter built-in server tool that searches the web for current information. The model decides when and how often to search. Works with any model that supports tool calling. If the selected model does not support tools calling, the legacy [Web Search Plugin](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/plugins/web-search) is used instead. 

Note: This option may increase cost due to external search usage (e.g. Exa, Parallel). 

Do NOT enable this option for models that already have built-in (native) web search, such as 'perplexity/sonar' or 'openai/gpt-4o-search-preview' - they do not require this setting. [Read more information](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/web-search).

params.title: Web Search: Engine
params.description:
Search engine for the server tool. 'auto' (default) uses native search if the provider supports it, otherwise Exa. 'native' forces the provider's built-in search. 'exa', 'parallel', and 'firecrawl' use external search services. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled. [Read more](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/web-search).

params.title: Web Search: Max Results
params.description:
Maximum number of search results to return per search call (1-25). Applies to Exa, Firecrawl, and Parallel engines; ignored with native provider search. Higher values provide more information but increase cost and token usage. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Search: Max Total Results
params.description:
Maximum total number of search results across all search calls in a single request. Useful for controlling cost and context size in agentic loops. Defaults to 50 when not specified. Ignored when Search Prompt is filled (legacy Web Search Plugin is used instead). 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Search: Context Size
params.description:
How much context to retrieve per result.

For models with built-in native web search (e.g. perplexity/sonar, openai/gpt-4o-search-preview), controls how much information is retrieved from each search. 

For other models: applies to Exa and Parallel engines; ignored with native provider search and Firecrawl. 

Ignored when Search Prompt is filled (legacy Web Search Plugin is used instead).

params.title: Web Search: Include Domains
params.description:
Limit search results to these domains. Supported by Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, and most native providers. Supports wildcards (e.g. `*.substack.com`) and path filtering (e.g. `openai.com/blog`). Cannot be used together with Search Exclude Domains. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Search: Exclude Domains
params.description:
Exclude search results from these domains. Supported by Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Anthropic, and xAI. Supports wildcards (e.g. `*.substack.com`) and path filtering (e.g. `openai.com/blog`). Cannot be used together with Search Include Domains. 

Available only when "Web Search" is enabled.

params.title: Web Fetch
params.description:
Server tool gives any model the ability to fetch content from a specific URL. When the model needs to read a web page or PDF document, it calls the tool with the URL. OpenRouter fetches and extracts the content, returning text that the model can use in its response.

Only available for models that support tools. Do NOT enable this option for models that already have built-in (native) web search, such as 'perplexity/sonar' or 'openai/gpt-4o-search-preview' - they do not require this setting.[See the documentation.](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/web-fetch)

params.title: Web Fetch Parameters JSON
params.description:
Optional configuration object. For example: {"engine":"auto","max_uses":5,"max_content_tokens":30000,"allowed_domains":["openrouter.ai"],"blocked_domains":["example.com"]}. 

Available only when "Web Fetch" is enabled. [See the documentation.](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/send-chat-completion-request#request.body.tools.WebFetchServerTool)

Useful for prompts that require temporal awareness - scheduling, time-sensitive questions, or any task where the model needs to know the current date and time. Works with any model that supports tool calling. [Read more information](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/datetime).

value.string:
## GEO Radar

Weekly AI search visibility monitor.

MAIN BRANCH (Schedule trigger)
read config and prompts -> build run matrix -> ask four engines
-> detect brand and competitor mentions -> write raw log
-> aggregate metrics per brand -> accumulate citation sources
-> check classic Google ranking -> generate an action plan
-> email the report, alert Slack on a drop.

SECOND BRANCH (Run once)
Prompt generator. Reads the brand homepage and writes 32
measurement questions into the prompts sheet.

All settings live in the Google Sheet, not in this scenario.
See README for the config columns.

Weekly AI search visibility monitor.

MAIN BRANCH (Schedule trigger)
read config and prompts -> build run matrix -> ask four engines
-> detect brand and competitor mentions -> write raw log
-> aggregate metrics per brand -> accumulate citation sources
-> check classic Google ranking -> generate an action plan
-> email the report, alert Slack on a drop.

SECOND BRANCH (Run once)
Prompt generator. Reads the brand homepage and writes 32
measurement questions into the prompts sheet.

All settings live in the Google Sheet, not in this scenario.
See README for the config columns.

params.title: Range

params.title: Filter JSON
params.description: Supports nested and/or filters; operators: `equal`, `not_equal`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `gt (greater than)`, `lt (less than)`, `gte (≥)`, `lte (≤)`, `exists`, `does_not_exist`; string comparisons are case-insensitive; operators `"exists"` and `"does_not_exist"` do not require a value field; example: { "type": "and", "rules": [ { "type": "or", "rules": [ { "column": "A", "operator": "equal", "value": "john" }, { "column": "E", "operator": "contains", "value": "admin" } ] }, { "column": "C", "operator": "gt", "value": "10" }, { "column": "D", "operator": "lte", "value": "100" }, { "column": "F", "operator": "exists" } ] }.

params.title: Quick preview schema
params.description:
This field lets you format response data for easy reading. Define key-path pairs in JSON, where the key is the header and the value is the data path.

Example: `{ "Name": "result.user.name", "Email": "result.contact.email" }`

params.title: Row Values
params.description: Provide an array of arrays. Each nested array should represent a row, with each element of the nested array representing a cell/column value (e.g., passing [["Foo",1,2],["Bar",3,4]] will insert two rows of data with three columns each). You can use an array from another Google Sheet Node result, e.g., [{{$3.result.response.values.[0]}}].
